name: neumorph-eyebrow

frames.best_why: Frames barely differ; frame 1 shows the top eyebrow and all three colour variants with no cursor.

tagline: Tiny embossed labels that sit above a heading.
summary: A short, pill-shaped label with a thin border and a soft pressed-in shadow, made to sit above a section heading. It comes in cream, pale blue and pale green.
appearance: Small fully rounded pills with a hairline border and a soft top-lit glow that makes them look pressed out of the surface. The default is cream with near-black text; the other two tint both fill and text pale blue or pale green.
behaviour: Static: nothing moves or responds. Each pill simply shows its short piece of text, and hovering or clicking does nothing.
demo_content: Labels Introducing Cult UI, Default, New release and v2.0 is live.
search_phrases: tiny pill label above a heading
pre heading pill for a landing page
use_when: You need a short pre-heading label that reads as a soft physical tag rather than a flat chip.
avoid_when: The text runs past a couple of words: the pill has a fixed height and will not wrap or grow.
customise: intent picks cream, blue or green, className adds classes, and children supply the text. All colours live in the variant map and need a source edit.
weight_why: Three small divs and a class map; nothing animates, loads or listens.

a11y.note: Plain text in a div reads correctly, but it carries no status or badge role for assistive tech.

issues: The demo's large heading dominates and the eyebrow is easy to overlook.
The pill has a fixed height, so a longer label will overflow rather than wrap.
polish_why: Clean soft-shadow pill, though at this size it reads as an ordinary tag.
title: Neumorph Eyebrow
